findings.title: Arbitrary local bytecode executed via ApoSkunkmanClassLoader.defineClass, auto-reloaded from skunkman.properties at every startup
findings.code_excerpt:
byte data[] = loadClassData(filename);
c = defineClass(data, 0, data.length);
findings.entry_point: (a) JFileChooser '.class' selection -> ApoSkunkmanPanel.loadPlayer(int,String) (game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:435-448); (b) persisted strings aiOne..aiFour read from user-editable ./skunkman.properties (ApoSkunkmanConstants.java:292-295) applied automatically at launch by ApoSkunkmanPanel.loadStartProperties/loadStartPlayer (game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:102-128)
findings.sink: defineClass(data,0,data.length) + c.newInstance() cast to ApoSkunkmanAI (ApoSkunkmanClassLoader.java:38-41), reached via new ApoSkunkmanClassLoader(path, classname).getAI() at game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:512
findings.data_path: skunkman.properties 'aiOne' -> ApoSkunkmanConstants.AI_ONE -> Panel.loadStartPlayer -> Panel.loadPlayer(player,s) parses 'path\Name.class' into source/playerName/className -> private loadPlayer(player,path,classname,classN) -> ApoSkunkmanClassLoader.getAI() -> loadClass -> loadClassData(new File(root,filename)) -> defineClass -> newInstance; constructor/static init and later ai.think()/ai.load()/ai.save() run with full JVM privileges (no SecurityManager anywhere in the tree)
findings.attack_scenario: The game is an AI-programming contest platform. An attacker posts a 'cool bot' zip containing Evil.class plus a skunkman.properties preset pointing aiOne at it. Victim extracts into the game dir and starts the game: the class instantiates before any gameplay, executing attacker code (file theft, reverse shell) with the victim's user rights. Alternatively anyone who can write to skunkman.properties (or swap the recorded path) turns the next launch into code execution.
findings.preconditions: Desktop run (loadPlayer returns early if ApoConstants.B_APPLET, ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:425-427); attacker-supplied .class on disk reachable at the recorded path; properties file in working directory is writable/plantable.
findings.validation_plan: Compile 'public class Evil extends apoSkunkman.ai.ApoSkunkmanAI' whose constructor does Files.write(Paths.get("pwned.txt"),"rce".getBytes()) (stub remaining abstract methods). Run the shipped jar, use the player 'load AI' button on Evil.class: pwned.txt appears. Then set aiOne=<abs-path>\Evil.class in skunkman.properties, relaunch: pwned.txt appears with zero interaction. Note also loadClass() is child-first (defineClass attempted before findSystemClass, lines 58-82), so a planted e.g. javax/swing class in the AI dir shadows application classes.

findings.title: URLClassLoader-based ApoClassLoader supports loading classes from a remote URL (applet branch) but has no caller in this variant
findings.entry_point: None wired up: repo-wide search shows ApoClassLoader is referenced nowhere outside its own file (only ApoSkunkmanClassLoader is used, at ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:512)
findings.sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass + c.newInstance() (lines 73-75) over a plain-HTTP URL when B_APPLET==true
findings.data_path: If ever called with B_APPLET=true: path string -> new URL(path) -> URLClassLoader -> loadClass -> newInstance. In the current build the call chain terminates: dead code inherited from the shared apogames library.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical: if a future/sibling wiring passes an http:// path while running as applet (where the sandbox would normally be the only barrier), getMyClass() fetches and executes bytecode from that host over plaintext HTTP, enabling a network MITM to serve malicious classes. In this variant nothing reaches it.
findings.preconditions: Someone must add a caller; would additionally require applet context or a codebase where B_APPLET is forced true. Java applet support itself is end-of-life.
findings.validation_plan: Verify absence: grep the whole tree for 'new ApoClassLoader' / 'getMyClass' - only the definition matches. To demonstrate the hazard if ever revived: host a jar with an ApoSkunkmanAI subclass on a local HTTP server, call new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/","Evil").getMyClass() with B_APPLET=true, watch tcpdump show plaintext GET and the constructor execute.

findings.title: Replay parser trusts attacker-controlled element count: unbounded allocation and NPE on truncated .rep files
findings.entry_point: 'Load replay' button -> ApoSkunkmanPanel.loadReplay() (game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:566-573) opens a user-selected .rep file (JFileChooser filter 'rep', ApoSkunkmanGameComponent.java:36,79-82) and hands it to replayIO.readLevel(path)
findings.sink: ArrayList<Byte> grown up to 2^31-1 iterations per player from ApoIO-provided DataInputStream (org/apogames/ApoIO.java:79-87); secondary sink: this.replay.setHelp(help) at ApoSkunkmanReplayIO.java:40 dereferences null if EOF struck before line 100
findings.data_path: .rep bytes -> FileInputStream (ApoIO.readLevel, ApoIO.java:79-81) -> ApoSkunkmanReplayIO.readLevel(DataInputStream): int players (offset ~22) then four loops of [readInt count + count bytes]. EOFException is swallowed upstream (ApoIO.java:88-89), so parsing 'succeeds' after allocating everything the file could feed; a header claiming huge sizes forces the loop to churn through the entire remaining stream boxing one Byte object per input byte (~16-24x amplification). If EOF hits before line 100, field 'replay' stays null and line 40 throws NullPointerException out of loadReplay onto the EDT.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker shares a tournament-looking .rep that is a valid 30-byte header (players=4) followed by size=0x3FFFFFFF and a few MB of filler. Victim loads it: heap fills with boxed Bytes, game freezes/OOMs (concrete crash under default -Xmx). A second file truncated right after the header instead kills the EDT with an NPE. Both are one-click crashes from a file someone asked you to 'watch my replay'.
findings.preconditions: Victim manually opens the crafted .rep via the replay dialog; desktop or applet alike (readLevel(String) uses disk path when !B_APPLET).
findings.validation_plan: Craft file: DataOutputStream.writeInt(any type)/writeLong/writeBoolean/writeInt(time)/writeInt(players=4)/writeUTF('')/4x writeUTF('') then writeInt(0x7FFFFFFF) + 5MB of 0x00, repeat; run 'java -jar -Xmx64m' and load it -> OutOfMemoryError/hang observable in jconsole. Second file ends after the names arrays -> console shows 'Exception in thread AWT-EventQueue' NullPointerException at ApoSkunkmanReplayIO.readLevel(String) line 40 and the UI dies.

findings.title: Level/replay editor data places players and goal at unvalidated byte coordinates, causing out-of-bounds array access and crash
findings.entry_point: (a) 'Load Editorlevel'/auto-load of levels/lastLevel.skunk -> ApoSkunkmanPanel.loadLevel (game/ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:597-610, auto-loaded at :109-111); (b) crafted .rep with embedded editor level -> ApoSkunkmanModelGame.startReplay -> level.loadAndMakeReplayLevel (game/ApoSkunkmanModelGame.java:334-344, level/ApoSkunkmanLevel.java:803-820)
findings.sink: OOB index into the fixed 15x15 level array at apoSkunkman/game/ApoSkunkmanModelEditor.java:202 (this.level[y][x][0] = PLAYER_ONE+i, y/x straight from getX()/TILE_SIZE during the mandatory makeEditorLevel() call at ApoSkunkmanPanel.java:606); second sink during play: level.getLevel()[y][x] at apoSkunkman/entity/ApoSkunkmanPlayer.java:498 before layBomb (:499), outside the try/catch that guards ai.think (:474-484)
findings.data_path: .skunk/.rep bytes -> EditorIO.readLevel reads signed bytes for 4 player positions (lines 47-52) and goalX (67-70) -> setX/setY store raw pixel offsets (can be -128*32 .. 127*32). For replays the same values ride through ApoSkunkmanReplayHelp Point array (replay/ApoSkunkmanReplayIO.java:75-81) -> ApoSkunkmanReplay.makeLevelFromHelp sets player positions (replay/ApoSkunkmanReplay.java:127-130). No range check exists between parse and use; canPlayerGo bounds-checks only the destination tile (level/ApoSkunkmanLevel.java:666-674), never the current one.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker distributes a 'custom map pack': patching one position byte to 0x7F makes loading the level itself throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException inside makeEditorLevel (instant crash on open). Variant B: coordinate 100 (in-bounds editor array, off-grid playfield) loads fine; once the round starts and that player lays a skunkman, ApoSkunkmanPlayer.thinkAI:498 indexes level[12][100] -> uncaught AIOOBE kills the game thread mid-tournament. Goal-point bytes likewise shift the win tile outside the grid so GoalX rounds can never be won.
findings.preconditions: Victim opens the crafted .skunk or plays the crafted .rep; no privilege needed - these are ordinary shared-content files.
findings.validation_plan: Hex-edit a valid lastLevel.skunk: byte at offset 5 (player 1 x) -> 0x7F. Launch, menu > Editor > Load: stack trace ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoSkunkmanModelEditor.makeEditorLevel(ModelEditor.java:202). Then set it to 100 (0x64, within byte range, outside 15-wide grid), start a match with that player AI-controlled, press the lay key when he is 'standing' off-grid: AIOOBE at ApoSkunkmanPlayer.thinkAI(Player.java:498) and the game window freezes/dies.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no java.io.ObjectInputStream (or XML/Kryo etc.) anywhere in the tree; save/level/replay formats are hand-written DataInputStream records
weak_integrity_check - no MessageDigest/MD5/hash or checksum logic at all (nothing to weaken; integrity simply doesn't exist, which is the root of ApoSkunkman-01/-03/-04)

insecure_transport - no live network code: the HttpURLConnection/URL branches in org/apogames/ApoIO.java:40-43,83-84 and ApoImage.java:91 are gated on ApoConstants.B_APPLET and are never invoked with URL strings in this variant (all call sites pass local file paths); no save_highscore.php/get_level.php endpoints exist here unlike sibling variants
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords, tokens, keys or identity strings are stored or transmitted

path_traversal - all file paths originate from JFileChooser dialogs (user.dir based, ApoSkunkmanGameComponent.java:63-96) or the CWD properties file; no untrusted string is ever used to construct a write path
information_disclosure - nothing in the variant sends data off-machine

legacy_sandbox_assumption - an applet entry point exists (apoSkunkman/ApoSkunkmanApplet.java) and B_APPLET correctly disables file IO and AI class loading (Panel.java:425-427, ApoSkunkmanConstants.loadProperties:188); no code assumes a granted SecurityManager elsewhere
notes: This is the cleanest variant to expect network findings in, and they are genuinely absent: ApoSkunkman ships no highscore/level-server client; its only networking is dormant library code (finding ApoSkunkman-02). The real attack surface is (1) the deliberate plugin mechanism - the game's whole purpose is executing untrusted contest AI jars/classes locally with zero sandboxing, and the chosen AI path is persisted in plaintext ./skunkman.properties and re-executed silently on every launch, making the properties file a persistence primitive (ApoSkunkman-01); and (2) hand-parsed .skunk/.rep content shared between players, which lacks both length caps and range checks (findings -03/-04). Two structural observations for the clone-and-own study: ApoSkunkmanClassLoader.java is a per-variant rename of the same loader template found in sibling variants, while org/apogames/help/ApoClassLoader.java is the shared-library twin carried along unused - the flaw template propagates through both channels. Also noteworthy: ApoSkunkmanPanel imports Stinker.StinkerMain (line 17, instantiated at :478) but no Stinker source exists in this tree, meaning an unauditable prebuilt third-party AI ('Stinker') ships inside the distributed jar and runs in-process like any other AI. AI code additionally receives an unrestricted ApoSkunkmanAILevel view of the whole level each tick and its load()/save() hooks receive the filesystem path (ai/ApoSkunkmanAI.java:41-51), so even 'honest' bots hold full file access under their own directory assumption only.
